mainTopic: Testing רב (one source) and לוי (two sources) against ברייתות, and the final ruling that the הלכה follows רב
overview: This amud continues the debate between רב, who says all of a woman's blood after childbirth comes from one source (מעין אחד), and לוי, who says pure and impure blood come from two separate sources (שני מעיינות). The גמרא tests both views against several ברייתות. Two sources seem hard for לוי: one requires seven clean days, and one requires a break of three עונות. Each time the גמרא answers that only a brief stop is needed. A ברייתא saying that a woman who sees blood after דם טוהר is impure only from that moment (דיה שעתה) seems hard for רב. The גמרא answers that there was no time gap, so there is nothing to backdate. A ברייתא about a יולדת בזוב whose blood is impure wet or dry challenges לוי again, and the גמרא gives two answers. Finally, מר זוטרא rules that we follow each of רב and לוי where he is strict. רב אשי and מרימר disagree, and the גמרא concludes that the הלכה follows רב, both to be lenient and to be strict.

steps.title: Why would לוי require seven clean days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges לוי: if pure and impure blood come from two different sources, a brief stop in bleeding should be enough, and seven fully clean days should not be needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to לוי, who says there are two separate sources, why do I need seven clean days? A tiny stop should be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to לוי and attacks his view using the ברייתא about a woman who gave birth while she was a זבה. That ברייתא requires her to sit seven clean days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי holds that once the days of impurity end, any later blood comes from the pure source. If so, even blood seen during her seven days should not cancel her count. A short stop after the impure days should therefore be enough, so why does the ברייתא demand seven truly clean days?

keyTerms.meaning: Two sources: לוי's view that pure blood and impure blood come from separate places
Seven clean days that a זבה must count before she becomes pure
Any tiny amount, here a brief moment of no bleeding
It is enough

phrases.english: But according to Levi, who said
they are two sources,
why do I need seven?
phrases.notes: The seven clean days the ברייתא required for a woman who gave birth while she was a זבה.

phrases.english: Any small amount should suffice!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְלֵוִי דְּאָמַר שְׁנֵי מַעְיָנוֹת הֵן, לְמָה לִי שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא contrast: the ברייתא about a woman who gave birth as a זבה fits רב's one-source view, but seems hard for לוי
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's view that there are שני מעיינות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under two sources, blood after the impure days is pure, so it should not cancel the count. Requiring seven fully clean days then seems unnecessary.

steps.title: She needs a brief stop, and then the seven days count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: she needs the bleeding to stop for a moment, and after that the next seven days count as her שבעה נקיים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא means: she needs the bleeding to stop for a moment, so that the following days will count for her as the seven clean days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends לוי by explaining what the ברייתא really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not demanding seven days with no blood at all. It only requires a short stop that marks the end of the impure days. After that stop, the next seven days count as her clean days, because any blood she sees then is pure blood. So the ברייתא fits לוי after all.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means: the גמרא is reinterpreting the source's wording
She should stop (the bleeding should stop)
So that they will count for her

steps.whatToRemember: According to לוי, the ברייתא only needs a brief break in bleeding after the impure days. After that, the seven days count as clean even if pure blood appears.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
she needs to stop for any small amount of time,
so that they will count for her as seven clean days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against לוי by rereading the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to demand seven fully blood-free days, which would not fit לוי
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only needs a brief stop, after which the seven days count as clean

steps.title: A new ברייתא: pregnancy days and nursing days combine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא teaching that blood-free days during pregnancy and during nursing can be added together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the days of her pregnancy count toward her nursing days, and the days of her nursing count toward her pregnancy days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new proof attempt by quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up the next move, and the actual point of the proof comes in step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pregnant or nursing woman who has gone three עונות without seeing blood is impure only from the moment she sees blood (דיה שעתה). This ברייתא adds that blood-free time from pregnancy and from nursing can be combined to reach those three עונות.

keyTerms.meaning: The days of her pregnancy
The days of her nursing
They count for her (they are added toward her total)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is only quoting the ברייתא at this point. Step 5 explains how it connects to the רב and לוי debate, so do not look for the proof here.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The days of her pregnancy count for her
phrases.notes: This means days of pregnancy in which she saw no blood.

phrases.english: toward the days of her nursing,
and the days of her nursing count for her
toward the days of her pregnancy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new proof attempt after the challenge against לוי was answered
steps.raayaObject: The debate over one source versus two sources (the proof is completed later)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about combining pregnancy and nursing days toward three עונות

steps.title: How the pregnancy and nursing days add up
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives examples: two עונות plus one, in either order, or one and a half plus one and a half, all add up to three עונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If she had no bleeding for two periods during pregnancy and one during nursing, or two during nursing and one during pregnancy, or one and a half during pregnancy and one and a half during nursing, they count for her as three periods.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and explains its rule with specific examples. The גמרא is still quoting its source before drawing the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any combination of blood-free time from pregnancy and nursing that totals three עונות is enough. The order does not matter, and even half-periods combine.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (introduces examples)
She stopped (had no bleeding)
Half
Three periods, each thirty days long, without seeing blood

phrases.english: How so?
If she stopped for two during her pregnancy days,
phrases.notes: 'Two' means two עונות, each thirty days long, with no bleeding.

phrases.english: and one during her nursing days;
two during her nursing days,
and one during her pregnancy days;
one and a half during her pregnancy days,
and one and a half during her nursing days —
they count for her as three periods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא, explaining its rule with examples
steps.raayaObject: The debate over one source versus two sources (the proof is completed later)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The examples in the ברייתא showing how pregnancy and nursing days combine

steps.title: Why would לוי need a three-period break?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא requires a break of שלש עונות. That fits רב's view of one source, but for לוי's view of two sources, a tiny break should be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רב, who says there is one source: that is why she needs a break of three עונות. But for לוי, who says there are two sources, why does she need a break of three עונות? A tiny break should be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at the ברייתא just quoted and argues that its demand for a three-עונות break fits רב but seems wrong according to לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, all the blood comes from one source, so pure blood still counts as 'seeing' and breaks the count. A real three-עונות stop is needed. For לוי, pure blood comes from a separate source and should not interrupt anything, so once the impure blood stops even for a moment, she should already count as having stopped.

keyTerms.meaning: Source (literally 'spring'): where the woman's blood comes from
A stop or break in the bleeding
An expected cycle period, roughly a month; three of them define a woman whose bleeding has stopped
Any tiny amount, here meaning a very short time

phrases.english: It makes sense according to Rav, who said:
It is one source,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי בָּעֵי הֶפְסֵק שָׁלֹשׁ עוֹנוֹת,
phrases.english: that is why she needs a break of three periods,
but according to Levi, who said:
They are two sources,
why do I need a break of three periods?
A tiny amount should be enough!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב דְּאָמַר מַעְיָן אֶחָד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from steps 3-4 to challenge לוי.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's view that pure and impure blood come from two sources.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If pure blood is a separate source, it cannot interrupt a break, so the ברייתא should not require three full עונות. A moment's stop should do.

steps.title: A short stop lets the pure days count toward three periods
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means she only needs a brief stop in the impure blood. After that, her days of purity count toward the three עונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא means: she needs the bleeding to stop for a moment, so that the following days will count for her toward the three עונות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for לוי by rereading the ברייתא so that it fits his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not demanding three blood-free עונות after the impure days. It only requires a tiny stop at the end of the impure days. After that, the days of purity count toward the three עונות, even if she sees pure blood during them, because that blood comes from a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means': the גמרא rereads a source
That they will count for her

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same move as step 2. The 'three עונות' are not a full break in bleeding. They are counted after a tiny stop, and pure blood seen during them does not ruin the count for לוי.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
She needs to stop for a tiny amount of time,
phrases.notes: This means the impure blood stops at the end of her impure days.

phrases.english: so that they will count for her toward three periods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to require three full עונות with no bleeding at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It requires only a moment's stop, after which the pure days count toward the three עונות.

steps.title: A new source: seeing blood after pure blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: all agree that a woman who sees blood after דם טוהר is impure only from the moment she sees it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: and they agree about a woman who sees blood after pure blood, that it is enough for her to be impure from her time of seeing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to test רב and לוי. This line sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, according to הלל, a woman who sees blood is impure backward in time. Here שמאי and הלל agree that after דם טוהר, she is impure only from the moment she sees the blood. This is the rule for a woman whose bleeding is treated as having stopped. The next step will ask which view explains this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree, meaning שמאי and הלל
Pure blood seen in the purity days after childbirth
Her time is enough: she is impure only from the moment she sees blood, not backward

phrases.english: Come and hear:
And they agree about a woman who sees blood after pure blood,
phrases.notes: 'They' are שמאי and הלל, who argue at the start of the מסכת about how far back impurity goes.

phrases.english: that her time is enough for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע וְשָׁוִין בְּרוֹאָה אַחַר דַּם טוֹהַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא to test the רב and לוי disagreement again.
steps.raayaObject: Which view, רב or לוי, fits the ruling of דיה שעתה after דם טוהר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the agreement of שמאי and הלל.

steps.title: Why would רב limit her impurity to the moment she sees?
steps.stepSummary: The rule דיה שעתה fits לוי, because pure blood does not interrupt her status. For רב, she just saw blood from the one source, so she should be impure מעת לעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for לוי, who says there are two sources: that is why her time is enough. But for רב, who says there is one source, why is her time enough? She should be impure for the past twenty-four hours!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the new ברייתא to challenge רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For לוי, the pure blood came from a different source. So she still counts as a woman whose bleeding stopped, and such a woman is impure only from the moment she sees. For רב, the pure blood came from the same single source, so she just saw blood. She should be treated like any woman and be impure backward for twenty-four hours (מעת לעת).

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (for one view), used to set up a challenge to the other view
Why?
From time to time: impure backward for the previous twenty-four hours

steps.whyThisMatters: Now the challenge has flipped. Earlier sources pressed לוי, but this ברייתא presses רב.

phrases.english: It makes sense according to Levi, who said:
They are two sources,
that is why her time is enough for her,
but according to Rav, who said:
It is one source,
why is her time enough for her?
She should be impure for twenty-four hours back!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְלֵוִי דְּאָמַר שְׁנֵי מַעְיָנוֹת הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 7 to challenge רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that all the blood comes from one source.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If pure blood comes from the same source, she has just seen blood and cannot count as a woman whose bleeding stopped. So she should be impure מעת לעת, not just from the moment she sees.

steps.title: No time gap, so there is nothing to backdate
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of דיה שעתה is a case where she saw blood right as her days of purity ended, with no time in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where there is no time gap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge against רב from step 8. The ברייתא is talking about a woman who saw blood immediately when her pure days ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a woman who sees blood is impure backward for the past twenty-four hours (מעת לעת). But here the past twenty-four hours were all inside her days of purity, so they cannot become impure. That is why she is impure only from now, even according to רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A gap of time
Where there is not

phrases.english: Where there is no time gap.
phrases.notes: No gap between the end of her pure days and the moment she saw blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 against רב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that even for רב, blood after pure days makes her impure only from now, against the usual מעת לעת rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is a case with no time gap, so the past twenty-four hours were all pure days and cannot be made impure.

steps.title: Why not impure from her last check?
steps.stepSummary: Even if she can't be impure for a full twenty-four hours, she should at least be impure back to her last self-check.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let her be impure from her last check until this check!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is another backdating rule: a woman is impure back to the last time she checked herself and found herself clean (מפקידה לפקידה). That last check could have been within a short time, so why does the ברייתא say she is impure only from the moment she saw blood?

keyTerms.meaning: From one self-check to the next; impurity reaching back to her last clean check
So let her be impure

phrases.english: But let her be impure from check to check!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that there is no time gap, so she is impure only from now.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'no gap' answer only removes the twenty-four-hour backdating. The separate rule of מפקידה לפקידה should still apply.

steps.title: חכמים did not make that rule here
steps.stepSummary: Since the twenty-four-hour backdating can't apply here, חכמים also did not apply the backdating to her last check.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there is no twenty-four-hour backdating in this case, the Rabbis also did not decree check-to-check impurity for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Backdating impurity is a rabbinic rule (גזירה). The two backdating rules go together, so where מעת לעת cannot apply, חכמים did not make מפקידה לפקידה apply either. So she really is impure only from the moment she sees blood.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis did not decree
Since
Also

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of דיה שעתה fits רב as well: there is no gap of time, so neither backdating rule applies.

phrases.english: Since there is no twenty-four-hour backdating,
also regarding check to check
the Rabbis did not decree on her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 and closes this line.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule of מפקידה לפקידה applies even when מעת לעת does not.
steps.terutzMaskana: חכמים linked the two rules. Where מעת לעת does not apply, they did not decree מפקידה לפקידה either.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: a יולדת בזוב who counted but did not immerse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a woman who gave birth as a זבה, counted her clean days, did not immerse, and then saw blood. בית שמאי and בית הלל each follow their usual view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a woman who gave birth while a זבה, who counted her clean days but did not immerse, and then saw blood: בית שמאי follow their view and בית הלל follow theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to test the argument between רב and לוי. The next step will show why it seems to cause trouble for לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a woman after birth who did not yet immerse, בית שמאי say her blood is impure only while wet, and בית הלל say it is impure whether wet or dry. The ברייתא says the same argument applies to a יולדת בזוב once she has counted her seven clean days.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who gave birth while she was a זבה
She counted her seven clean days
She immersed in a מקוה
According to their own view

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A woman who gave birth as a זבה, who counted
but did not immerse, and she saw blood,
בית שמאי follow their view,
phrases.notes: Their view about a woman after birth who didn't immerse: her blood is impure only while wet.

phrases.english: and בית הלל follow their view.
phrases.notes: Their view: the blood is impure whether wet or dry.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: יוֹלֶדֶת בְּזוֹב שֶׁסָּפְרָה וְלֹא טָבְלָה וְרָאֲתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the last challenge was answered, the גמרא opens a new proof attempt about רב and לוי.
steps.raayaObject: The argument between רב (one מעין) and לוי (two מעיינות).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a יולדת בזוב who counted but did not immerse.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits רב but seems hard for לוי
steps.stepSummary: For רב, all the blood comes from one source, so it is impure wet or dry. For לוי, blood after counting comes from the pure source, so why is it impure wet or dry?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רב, who said there is one source; that is why it is impure wet or dry. But for לוי, who said there are two sources, why is it impure wet or dry?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא of step 12 to challenge לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, she has not immersed yet, so the blood from the single source still carries impurity, and בית הלל's wet-or-dry rule makes sense. For לוי, once she counted her clean days, new blood should come from the pure source, so it should not be impure at all, and surely not when dry.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for (this view)
Source, spring (of blood)
Wet and dry
Why?

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about בית שמאי. It is about בית הלל's ruling that the blood is impure even when dry, which is hard to explain for לוי.

phrases.english: It works well for רב, who said:
It is one source,
that is why it makes impure, wet or dry.
But for לוי, who said:
They are two sources,
why does it make impure, wet or dry?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב, דְּאָמַר: מַעְיָן אֶחָד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא of step 12 to challenge לוי.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's view that there are two separate sources.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If blood after her counted days comes from the pure source, it should not be impure. Yet בית הלל rule that it is impure even when dry.

steps.title: לוי follows a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: לוי answers that he holds like the תנא who says שמאי and הלל agree (step 7), which fits his two-sources view.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי can say to you: What I said follows the תנא who says they agree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא from step 13 for לוי. לוי says this ברייתא is not his source, because he follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא about a woman who gave birth as a זבה seems to treat all the blood as coming from one source. לוי says he holds like the other תנא quoted earlier (step 7), who says שמאי and הלל agree that a woman who sees blood after seeing pure blood (דם טוהר) is impure only from the moment she sees it (דיה שעתה). That view treats the blood of the days of purity as coming from a separate source, which is exactly לוי's opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period whose teaching is quoted
They agree. Here it means שמאי and הלל agree, as in step 7.

phrases.english: Levi can say to you:
What I said follows the tanna who says they agree.
phrases.notes: That's the ברייתא from step 7, where שמאי and הלל agree that blood seen after pure blood makes her impure only from when she saw it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא against לוי from step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a different תנא (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא about a woman who gave birth as a זבה seemed to disprove לוי's view of two sources
steps.terutzMaskana: לוי is not bound by that ברייתא. He follows the תנא of שָׁוִין, who supports two sources.

steps.title: Or: She bled without stopping
steps.stepSummary: A second answer for לוי: the ברייתא is about a woman whose bleeding flowed nonstop from her impure days into her pure days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: the case is a woman who bleeds continuously.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to defend לוי. The ברייתא may be speaking about a woman whose bleeding never stopped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the flow started in her days of impurity and simply kept going into her days of purity, then the blood is still the same impure blood. Even לוי agrees that such blood is impure. So the ברייתא no longer contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman whose bleeding flows continuously without stopping
And if you want, say: introduces an alternative answer

phrases.english: And if you want, say: it is about a woman who bleeds continuously,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the same קשיא from step 13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The blood she saw in her days of purity seemed to be new blood from the pure source
steps.terutzMaskana: The blood is a continuation of the impure flow, so even לוי agrees it is impure

steps.title: But the ברייתא says she counted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the ברייתא says she counted clean days, so her bleeding did stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches that she 'counted'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of a nonstop flow. The ברייתא clearly says she counted her clean days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting clean days means she had days with no bleeding. That seems impossible if her bleeding never stopped. So the 'continuous flow' answer does not seem to fit the words of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: She counted her seven clean days, with no bleeding
It teaches. This points to the exact wording of the source.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'she counted'!
phrases.notes: Counting means seven clean days with no blood, so how could her bleeding have been nonstop?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 15 that the woman bled continuously
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'she counted' shows she had clean days, which contradicts a nonstop flow

steps.title: A mother of a girl whose second week did not stop
steps.stepSummary: The case is a woman who gave birth to a girl while a זבה. Her bleeding stopped in the first week but continued through the second week into her days of purity. Her clean birth days count toward her זיבה count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a woman who gave birth to a girl while she was a זבה. In the first week her bleeding stopped, but in the second week it did not stop. And this תנא holds that the days after birth on which she sees no blood count toward the counting of her זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how she could both 'count' and still have a nonstop flow. It describes a very specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After giving birth to a girl, a woman has two weeks of impurity. She had seven clean days in the first week, and they count as her זיבה count, so the ברייתא can say she 'counted'. In the second week the bleeding came back and flowed nonstop into her days of purity, so that blood still comes from the impure source, and לוי agrees it is impure.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who gave birth to a girl, which brings two weeks of birth impurity
While she was a זבה, having irregular bleeding
She stopped bleeding
The counting of seven clean days needed to end her זיבה status
Her days of birth impurity

steps.confusionAlert: Both things happened in different weeks. The 'counting' was in the first week, and the nonstop flow was in the second week. The blood in her days of purity continues the second week's flow.
steps.whatToRemember: לוי survives the challenge: the ברייתא is about blood that is a continuation of the impure flow, not new blood from the pure source.

phrases.english: Here we are dealing with a woman who gave birth to a girl while a zava,
where in the first week she stopped bleeding,
but in the second week she did not stop,

phrases.english: and he holds: the days of her birth impurity on which she sees no blood
phrases.notes: 'He' is the תנא of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: count for her toward the counting of her ziva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 16 and saves the answer of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) plus identifying the תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'She counted' seemed to rule out a continuous flow
steps.terutzMaskana: She counted in week one (clean birth days count for זיבה), and the flow in week two continued into her days of purity

steps.title: מר זוטרא: the הלכה follows both רב and לוי to be strict
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא ruled that the הלכה follows רב where he is strict and לוי where he is strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: רב שמן from סכרא told us that מר זוטרא came to our town and taught: The הלכה follows רב to be strict, and the הלכה follows לוי to be strict.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא reports that מר זוטרא gave a practical ruling on the מחלוקת between רב and לוי: take the strict side of each opinion. רב אשי disagrees, and the final ruling goes the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רב, if a flow from her days of purity continues past their end, the blood after the end is impure. Following לוי, if a flow from her days of impurity continues into her days of purity, that blood is impure. In each case we pick whichever view makes the blood impure.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law
To be strict
He taught publicly

steps.whatToRemember: מר זוטרא's ruling: follow רב and לוי only where each is strict, so the blood is treated as impure in both kinds of continuous flow. The final הלכה, though, follows רב both to be lenient and to be strict.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical bottom line for the long debate between רב (one source) and לוי (two sources).

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Rav Shemen from Sikhra told us:
Mar Zutra happened to come to our town, and he taught:
The halacha follows Rav to be strict,
and the halacha follows Levi to be strict.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final practical ruling on the רב–לוי debate after לוי's view has been defended
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מר זוטרא ruled that the הלכה follows each of רב and לוי where he is strict, so continuous blood is treated as impure in both directions. The גמרא's final word rejects this: the הלכה follows רב both to be lenient and to be strict.

steps.title: רב אשי rules the הלכה follows רב in every case
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי disagrees with מר זוטרא and rules that the הלכה follows רב fully, both where it is lenient and where it is strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The הלכה follows רב, both when that means being lenient and when it means being strict.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different ruling from מר זוטרא. He says we follow רב all the way, not only where רב is stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא picked the strict side of each opinion, so a woman would have to follow both רב and לוי. רב אשי rejects that mix and says to follow רב's view fully. Where רב's view gives a lenient result, we are lenient, even if לוי would be stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows his opinion
To be lenient, the easier outcome
To be strict, the harder outcome

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with מר זוטרא. He said to follow רב and לוי wherever each is strict. רב אשי says to follow only רב, even where רב is lenient.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rav,
whether as a leniency or as a stringency.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הִלְכְתָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing ruling to מר זוטרא's 'follow each one where he is strict'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רב in every case, for both leniency and stringency.

steps.title: מרימר publicly teaches the same ruling
steps.stepSummary: מרימר taught in a public lecture that the הלכה follows רב, both to be lenient and to be strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר taught publicly: The הלכה follows רב, both when that means being lenient and when it means being strict.
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage, מרימר, says the same thing as רב אשי. He taught it in a public lecture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now two sages, not just one, back following רב completely. Because מרימר taught it publicly, this was meant as a ruling for people to follow in practice. This adds weight against מר זוטרא's mixed approach.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught publicly, gave this ruling in a lecture to the community

phrases.english: Mareimar taught publicly:
The halakha is in accordance with Rav,
whether as a leniency or as a stringency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אשי's ruling with an identical public teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רב, both for leniency and stringency, as taught in public.

steps.title: Final ruling: the הלכה follows רב completely
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives its own final decision: the הלכה follows רב, both to be lenient and to be strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows רב, both when that means being lenient and when it means being strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא itself closes the discussion and decides the matter. We follow רב in every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line has no sage's name on it, so it is the גמרא's own final word. It sides with רב אשי and מרימר rather than מר זוטרא. So we do not follow לוי's view even where it is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: And the law is, the גמרא's own closing ruling with no name on it

steps.whatToRemember: Three views were given: מר זוטרא said to follow whoever is stricter, while רב אשי and מרימר said to follow רב completely. The גמרא's final ruling follows רב, both to be lenient and to be strict.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law for the whole רב and לוי discussion, so the cases discussed earlier are decided according to רב.

phrases.english: And the halakha is in accordance with Rav,
whether as a leniency or as a stringency.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב, בֵּין לְקוּלָּא בֵּין לְחוּמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between מר זוטרא and רב אשי and מרימר, siding with the latter two.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The final הלכה follows רב in all cases, whether the result is lenient or strict.
